questions.question: Two objects are projected with same velocity $u$ however at different angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with the horizontal. If $\alpha + \beta = 90 ^\circ$, the ratio of horizontal range of the first object to the ${2}^{\mathrm{nd}}$ object will be :
questions.explanation:
Given: $\alpha + \beta = 90 ^\circ$

Range of the first projectile:

${R}_{1} = \frac{{u}^{2}\sin 2\alpha }{g}$

Range of the second projectile:

${R}_{2} = \frac{{u}^{2}\sin 2\beta }{g}\;$

As we can see, both are equal.

${R}_{1} = {R}_{2}$

Therefore,

${R}_{1} : {R}_{2} = 1 : 1$

questions.question: The angle of projection of a particle is measured from the vertical axis as $\phi$ and the maximum height reached by the particle is $h_m$. Here $h_m$ as function of $\phi$ can be presented as
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{H}_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \cos ^2 \phi}{2 \mathrm{~g}}$

questions.question: The co-ordinates of a particle moving in $x-y$ plane are given by : $x=2+4 \mathrm{t}, y=3 \mathrm{t}+8 \mathrm{t}^2$. The motion of the particle is :
options: uniformly accelerated having motion along a parabolic path.
uniform motion along a straight line.
uniformly accelerated having motion along a straight line.
questions.explanation:
$\begin{aligned} & x=2+4 t \\ & \frac{d x}{d t}=v_x=4 \\ & \frac{d v_x}{d t}=a_x=0 \\ & y=3 t+8 t^2 \\ & \frac{d y}{d t}=v_y=3+16 t \\ & \frac{d v_y}{d t}=a_y=16 \end{aligned}$ the motion will be uniformly accelerated motion. For path $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}=2+4 \mathrm{t} \\ & \frac{(\mathrm{x}-2)}{4}=\mathrm{t} \end{aligned}$

Put this value of $t$ is equation of $y y=3\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)+8\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)^2$ this is a quadratic equation so path will be parabola.

questions.question: A projectile is projected at $30 ^\circ$ from horizontal with initial velocity $40m{s}^{ - 1}$. The velocity of the projectile at $t = 2s$ from the start will be:
questions.explanation:
It is given that $v = 40m{s}^{ - 1}$.

The components of the velocity will be ${v}_{y} = v\sin 30 ^\circ = \frac{40m{s}^{ - 1}}{2} = 20m{s}^{ - 1}\;$

The time taken to reach maximum height is $T = \frac{u\sin 30 ^\circ }{g} = \frac{20m{s}^{ - 1}}{10m{s}^{ - 2}} = 2s$

Hence, at $T = 2s,\text{as}{v}_{y} = 0m{s}^{ - 1}\text{therefore}{v}_{net} = {v}_{x} = 20\sqrt{3}m{s}^{ - 1}$.

questions.question: A particle moving in a circle of radius $R$ with uniform speed takes time $T$ to complete one revolution. If this particle is projected with the same speed at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it is equal to $4R$. The angle of projection $\theta$ is then given by :
questions.explanation:
Time period of circular motion is given by,

$\frac{2\pi R}{v} = T\;$

Now, maximum height $H = \frac{{v}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta }{2g} \implies 4R = \frac{4{\pi }^{2}{R}^{2}}{{T}^{2}}\frac{{\sin }^{2}\theta }{2g} \implies \sin \theta = \sqrt{\frac{2g{T}^{2}}{{\pi }^{2}R}} \implies \theta = {\sin }^{−1}{\left(\frac{2g{T}^{2}}{{\pi }^{2}R}\right)}^{\frac{1}{2}}$

;

questions.question: A helicopter is flying horizontally with a speed $v$ at an altitude $h$ has to drop a food packet for a man on the ground. What is the distance of helicopter from the man when the food packet is dropped ?
questions.explanation: The aeroplane imparts $v$ velocity to the food packet horizontally when dropping. Horizontal range of food packet $= v \times \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$ Also, Horizontal distance, travelled by aeroplane $= v \times \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$ thus, vertical distance between aeroplane and person $= h$ distance $= \sqrt{\frac{2{v}^{2}h}{g} + {h}^{2}}$ ,

questions.question: A child stands on the edge of the cliff $10m$ above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with an initial speed of $5m{s}^{–1}$ . Neglecting the air resistance, the speed with which the stone hits the ground will be _____ $m{s}^{–1}$ (given, $g = 10m{s}^{–2}$ ).
questions.explanation: Given here, $u = 5m{s}^{ - 1},h = 10m$ Using ${v}_{y}^{2} = {u}_{y}^{2} + 2gh$ in vertical direction, we have the velocity of stone in vertical direction as ${v}_{y} = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{200}m{s}^{ - 1}$ (since, ${u}_{y} = 0$). The final velocity along the horizontal direction is the same as the initial horizontal velocity as there is no acceleration along the x-axis. The speed with which the stone hits the ground is ${v}_{net} = \sqrt{{v}_{x}^{2} + {v}_{y}^{2}} = \sqrt{25 + 200} = 15m{s}^{ - 1}$ `

questions.question: The maximum height reached by a projectile is $64 \mathrm{~m}$. If the initial velocity is halved, the new maximum height of the projectile is _____ $\mathrm{m}$.
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{H}_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{H}_{1 \text { max }}}{\mathrm{H}_{2 \max }}=\frac{\mathrm{u}_1^2}{\mathrm{u}_2^2} \\ & \frac{64}{\mathrm{H}_{2 \max }}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{(\mathrm{u} / 2)^2} \\ & \mathrm{H}_{2 \max }=16 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A fighter jet is flying horizontally at a certain altitude with a speed of $200{ms}^{ - 1}$. When it passes directly overhead an anti-aircraft gun, a bullet is fired from the gun, at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal, to hit the jet. If the bullet speed is $400m{s}^{ - 1}$, the value of $\theta$ will be _____ $^\circ$.
questions.explanation: In order to hit, horizontal velocity of both moving object should be same, ${V}_{1} = {V}_{2}\cos \theta \implies 200 = 400\cos \theta \implies \cos \theta = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = 60 ^\circ$$$

questions.question: A particle is projected with velocity $u$ so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as $\frac{n u^2}{25 g}$, where value of $n$ is : (Given ' $g$ ' is the acceleration due to gravity).
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Range }=3 \mathrm{H}_{\max } \\ & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\mathrm{~g}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}}\end{aligned} 2 \sin \theta \cos \theta=\frac{3}{2} \sin ^2 \theta \tan \theta=\frac{4}{3} \Rightarrow \theta=53^{\circ} \mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2\left(2 \times \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{4}{5}\right)}{\mathrm{g}} \Rightarrow \frac{24 \mathrm{u}^2}{25 \mathrm{~g}}$

questions.question: Two projectiles are projected at $30 ^\circ$ and $60 ^\circ$with the horizontal with the same speed. The ratio of the maximum height attained by the two projectiles respectively is:
questions.explanation:
The maximum height is given by, $H = \frac{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta }{2g}$.

The given data is

${\theta }_{1} = 30 ^\circ \;$

Therefore,

$\frac{{\left({H}_{1}\right)}_{max}}{{\left({H}_{2}\right)}_{max}} = \frac{{u}_{1}^{2}{\sin }^{2}{\theta }_{1}}{{u}_{2}^{2}{\sin }^{2}{\theta }_{2}}\;$

questions.question: A particle starts from the origin at $t = 0$ with an initial velocity of $3.0\hat{i}m / s$ and moves in the $x - y$ plane with a constant acceleration $\left(6.0\hat{i} + 4.0\hat{j}\right)m / {s}^{2}.$ The $x -$ coordinate of the particle at the instant when its $y -$ coordinate is $32m$ is $D$ meters. The value of $D$ is:

Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles $\left(45^{\circ}+\alpha\right)$ and $\left(45^{\circ}-\alpha\right)$ with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.explanation:
$\theta_1=45+\alpha ; \theta_2=45-\alpha$

Time of flight, $\mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \mathrm{v} \sin \theta}{\mathrm{g}} \frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\sin (45+\alpha)}{\sin (45-\alpha)} \frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha} \frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\cos \alpha+\sin \alpha}{\cos \alpha-\sin \alpha}=\frac{1+\tan \alpha}{1-\tan \alpha}$

questions.question: The ranges and heights for two projectiles projected with the same initial velocity at angles $42 ^\circ$ and $48 ^\circ$ with the horizontal are ${R}_{1},{R}_{2}$ and ${H}_{1},{H}_{2}$ respectively. Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Range$R = \frac{{u}^{2}\sin 2\theta }{g}$ and same for $\theta$ and $90 - \theta$. So, same for $42 ^\circ$ and $48 ^\circ$ Maximum height $H = \frac{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta }{2g}$, so height is high for higher $\theta$. So, $H$ for $48 ^\circ$ is higher than $H$ for $42 ^\circ$. ;

questions.question: A plane is inclined at an angle $\alpha = 30 ^\circ$ with respect to the horizontal. A particle is projected with a speed $u = 2m{s}^{ - 1}$ , from the base of the plane, making an angle $\theta = 15 ^\circ$ with respect to the plane as shown in the figure. The distance from the base, at which the particle hits the plane is close to: (Take $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$ )
questions.explanation: Range $= \frac{2{u}^{2}sin\alpha \cos ⁡\left(\alpha + \theta \right)}{g{\cos }^{2}⁡\theta } \alpha = angleofinclination = 30 ^\circ \theta = angleofprojectionfrominclination = 15 ^\circ u = 2m / s R = \frac{2{\left(2\right)}^{2}sin15 ^\circ \cos ⁡\left(15 ^\circ + 30 ^\circ \right)}{g{\cos }^{2}⁡30 ^\circ } = \frac{8\sin ⁡15 ^\circ cos45 ^\circ }{gco{s}^{2}30 ^\circ } \left(sin15 ^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right) R = \frac{4}{5}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{3}\right) \approx 0.2m R \approx 20cm$ `

questions.question: Projectiles $A$ and $B$ are thrown at angles of $45 ^\circ$ and $60 ^\circ$ with vertical respectively from top of a $400m$ high tower. If their times of flight are same, the ratio of their speeds of projection ${v}_{A} : {v}_{B}$ is:
questions.explanation:
For same time of flight, vertical component of velocity of projection must be same. Therefore,

${v}_{A}\sin 45 ^\circ = {v}_{B}\sin 30 ^\circ \;$

!

questions.question: A ball is projected with kinetic energy $E$, at an angle of $60 ^\circ$ to the horizontal. The kinetic energy of this ball at the highest point of its flight will become :
questions.explanation: $E = \frac{1}{2}m{u}^{2}$ At the Highest point, velocity is equal to the horizontal component of the velocity of projection. Therefore, $v = u\cos 60 ^\circ = \frac{u}{2} ∴$ Kinetic energy at the topmost point $= \frac{1}{2}m{\left(\frac{u}{2}\right)}^{2} = \frac{E}{4}$ `

questions.question: A body of mass $M$ thrown horizontally with velocity $v$ from the top of the tower of height $H$ touches the ground at a distance of $100 \mathrm{~m}$ from the foot of the tower. A body of mass $2 \mathrm{M}$ thrown at a velocity $\frac{v}{2}$ from the top of the tower of height $4 \mathrm{H}$ will touch the ground at a distance of _____$\mathrm{m}$.
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & 100=v \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}}} ; \quad \mathrm{x}=\frac{v}{2} \sqrt{\frac{2(4 \mathrm{H})}{\mathrm{g}}}=v \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=100\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A body is projected from the ground at an angle of $45 ^\circ$ with the horizontal. Its velocity after $2s$ is $20{ms}^{ - 1}$. The maximum height reached by the body during its motion is _____ $m$. (use $g = 10{ms}^{ - 2}$)
questions.explanation: After $2s$ the velocity is $20m{s}^{ - 1} \implies {v}_{x}^{2} + {v}_{y}^{2} = {v}^{2} = 400 \implies {u}^{2}{\cos }^{2}45 ^\circ + {\left(u\sin 45 ^\circ - gt\right)}^{2} = \frac{{u}^{2}}{2} + {\left(\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}} - 20\right)}^{2} = 400 \implies \frac{{u}^{2}}{2} + \frac{{u}^{2}}{2} + 400 - \frac{40}{\sqrt{2}}u = 400 \implies {u}^{2} = \frac{40}{\sqrt{2}}u \implies u = \frac{40}{\sqrt{2}}m{s}^{ - 1}$ Now the maximum height of the projectile is given by, $H = \frac{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta }{2g}\;$

questions.question: The maximum vertical height to which a man can throw a ball is $136m$. The maximum horizontal distance upto which he can throw the same ball is
questions.explanation:
Maximum height is achieved when the projection is along the vertical direction,

${H}_{max} = \frac{{v}^{2}}{2g} = 136m$

Now, for maximum range, angle of projection should be $45 ^\circ$. Therefore,

${R}_{max} = \frac{{v}^{2}}{g}\; = 2\left(136\right) = 272m$

questions.question: A bomb is dropped by a fighter plane flying horizontally. To an observer sitting in the plane, the trajectory of the bomb is a :
options: straight line vertically down the plane
parabola in a direction opposite to the motion of plane
parabola in the direction of motion of plane
questions.explanation: The bomb after being dropped from the plane will have only horizontal velocity but zero vertical velocity. This scenario is as same as if a body is horizontally projected from the top of a tower, and it hits the ground tracing a parabolic path. Hence, the trajectory of the bomb is also a parabola, in the direction of motion of the plane. But if we look the trajectory with respect to observer sitting in the plane then this looks like straight line vertically down the plane due to same horizontal velocity.

questions.question: Two projectiles are fired with same initial speed from same point on ground at angles of $\left(45^{\circ}-\alpha\right)$ and $\left(45^{\circ}+\alpha\right)$, respectively, with the horizontal direction. The ratio of their maximum heights attained is :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{Max}}=\frac{(\mathrm{u} \sin \theta)^2}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \frac{\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_1}{\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_2}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2(45-\alpha)}{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2(45+\alpha)} \\ & =\frac{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha\right)^2}{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha\right)^2} \\ & =\frac{1-\sin 2 \alpha}{1+\sin 2 \alpha}\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A shell is fired from a fixed artillery gun with an initial speed u such that it hits the target on the ground at a distance $R$ from it. If ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$ are the values of the time taken by it to hit the target in two possible ways, the product ${t}_{1}{t}_{2}$ is:
questions.explanation:
We know for complementary angle range is same for same projection speed.

${t}_{1} = \frac{2usin(\theta )}{g}$ ….. (i)

${t}_{2} = \frac{2usin(90 - \theta )}{g}$ ….. (ii)

$R = \frac{2{u}^{2}si\mathrm{nθc}os\theta }{g}$ .… (iii)

From equation (i) and (ii)

${t}_{1}{t}_{2} = \frac{4\text{ }{U}^{2}sin\theta \text{ }cos\theta }{{g}^{2}}$

(Using the value of R from equation iii)

${t}_{1}{t}_{2} = \frac{2R}{g}$

questions.question: The angle of projection for a projectile to have same horizontal range and maximum height is :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & 4 \sin \theta \cos \theta=\sin ^2 \theta \\ & 4=\tan \theta\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A projectile is launched at an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal with a velocity $20{ms}^{ - 1}$. After $10s$, its inclination with horizontal is $\beta$. The value of $\tan \beta$ will be : $\left(g = 10{ms}^{ - 2}\right)$.
questions.explanation: Component of velocity in horizontal direction, ${v}_{x} = 20\cos \alpha = {v}_{2}\cos \beta$ Component of velocity in vertical direction, ${v}_{y} = 20\sin \alpha - g \times 10 = {v}_{2}\sin \beta \implies \tan \beta = \frac{20\sin \alpha - 100}{20\cos \alpha } \implies \tan \beta = \tan \alpha - \frac{5}{\cos \alpha } \implies \tan \beta = \tan \alpha - 5\sec \alpha$ .

questions.question: A player kicks a football with an initial speed of $25{ms}^{ - 1}$ at an angle of $45 ^\circ$ from the ground. What are the maximum height and the time taken by the football to reach at the highest point during motion? (Take $g = 10{ms}^{ - 2}$)
questions.explanation:
$\theta = 45 ^\circ H = \frac{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta }{2g} = \frac{(25{)}^{2} \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2 \times 10} = \frac{125}{8}\text{m}$

and time $t = \frac{T}{2} = \frac{u\sin \theta }{g} = \frac{25\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{10} = \frac{25}{10\sqrt{2}} = \frac{5}{2\sqrt{2}}\text{s}$

,

questions.question:
A body of mass $10\mathrm{kg}$ is projected at an angle of $45 ^\circ$ with the horizontal. The trajectory of the body is observed to pass through a point $\left(20,10\right)$. If $T$ is the time of flight, then its momentum vector, at time $t = \frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}$, is _____ .

[Take $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$]
questions.explanation:
It is given that the projectile passes through $\left(20,10\right)$ and angle of projection is $\theta = 45 ^\circ$. Using the trajectory equation,

$y = x\tan \theta - \frac{g{x}^{2}}{2{u}^{2}{\cos }^{2}\theta } \implies 10 = 20 - \frac{\left(10\right)\left(100\right)}{{u}^{2}} \implies u = 20m{s}^{ - 1}$

Now the time of flight of projectile,

$T = \frac{2u\sin \theta }{g} \implies T = \frac{\left(2\right)\left(20\right)}{\sqrt{2}\left(10\right)} = 2\sqrt{2}s\;$

Now velocity of the projectile at any time $t$ can be written as,

$\vec{v} = u\cos \theta \hat{i} + \left(u\sin \theta - gt\right)\hat{j} \implies \vec{v} = 10\sqrt{2}\hat{i} + (10\sqrt{2} - 10\left(2\right)]\hat{j}m{s}^{ - 1}$

Therefore, momentum $\vec{p} = M\vec{v} = 100\sqrt{2}\hat{i} + \left(100\sqrt{2} - 200\right)\hat{j}Ns$

;

questions.question: Two guns $A$ and $B$ can fire bullets at speeds $1km / s$ and $2km / s$ respectively. From a point on a horizontal ground, they are fired in all possible directions. The ratio of maximum areas covered by the bullets fired by the two guns, on the ground is:

Two balls with same mass and initial velocity, are projected at different angles in such a way that maximum height reached by first ball is 8 times higher than that of the second ball. $T_1$ and $T_2$ are the total flying times of first and second ball, respectively, then the ratio of $T_1$ and $T_2$ is :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, }\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_1=8 \times\left(\mathrm{H}_{\max }\right)_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta_1}{2 \mathrm{~g}}=8 \times \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta_2}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \theta_1=2 \sqrt{2} \sin \theta_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{u} \sin \theta_1 / \mathrm{g}}{2 \mathrm{u} \sin \theta_2 / \mathrm{g}}=\frac{\sin \theta_1}{\sin \theta_2}=2 \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$ `

questions.question: A body is projected at $t=0$ with a velocity $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at $t=1$ s is $R$. Neglecting air resistance and taking acceleration due to gravity $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, the value of $R$ is:
questions.explanation: Horizontal component of velocity $\mathrm{v}_{x}=10 \cos 60^{\circ}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ vertical component of velocity $v_{y}=10 \cos 30^{\circ}=5 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ After $\mathrm{t}=1 \mathrm{sec}$ Horizontal component of velocity $\mathrm{v}_{x}=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Vertical component of velocity $v_{y}=|(5 \sqrt{3}-10)| \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}=10-5 \sqrt{3}$ Centripetal, acceleration $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^{2}}{\mathrm{R}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}^{2}+\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}}=\frac{25+100+75-100 \sqrt{3}}{10 \cos \theta}$ From figure (using (i)) $\tan \theta=\frac{10-5 \sqrt{3}}{5}=2-\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \theta=15^{\circ} \mathrm{R}=\frac{100(2-\sqrt{3})}{10 \cos 15}=2.8 \mathrm{~m}$ ,

questions.question: The initial speed of a projectile fired from ground is $u$. At the highest point during its motion, the speed of projectile is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}u$. The time of flight of the projectile is:
questions.explanation: At maximum height, only horizontal velocity of the particle remains. Let the angle of project be $\theta$. The horizontal velocity of the particle will remain same, therefore $u\cos \theta = \frac{\sqrt{3}u}{2}\;$ Now, time of flight of projectile is $T = \frac{2u\sin \theta }{g} = \frac{u}{g}$ !

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ projected with a velocity $u$ making an angle of $30 ^\circ$ with the horizontal. The magnitude of angular momentum of the projectile about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height $h$ is :
questions.explanation:
Angular momentum at maximum height will be, $L = \left(mu\cos \theta \right)h$, where $h =$maximum height

Therefore, $L = mu\cos \theta \times \frac{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta }{2g} = \frac{m{u}^{3}}{2g} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times {\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}m{u}^{3}}{16g}$

!

questions.question: A projectile is projected with velocity of $25m{s}^{ - 1}$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. After $t$ seconds its inclination with horizontal becomes zero. If $R$ represents horizontal range of the projectile, the value of $\theta$ will be : [use $\mathrm{use}g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$]
questions.explanation:
From the information given in the question, after time $t$ the inclination of the projectile becomes zero i.e. the projectile is at the highest point. Therefore,

$t = \frac{T}{2} = \frac{u\sin \theta }{g}$.

The rang of the projectile $R = \frac{2{u}^{2}\sin \theta \cos \theta }{g}$.

Now,

$\frac{R}{{t}^{2}} = \frac{2{u}^{2}\sin \theta \cos \theta }{g} \times \frac{{g}^{2}}{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta } = 2g\cot \theta \;$

`

questions.question: The trajectory of a projectile near the surface of the earth is given as $y = 2x - 9{x}^{2}.$ If it were launched at an angle ${\theta }_{0}$ with speed ${v}_{0}$ then $\left(g = 10{ms}^{ - 2}\right) :$
questions.explanation:
$y = 2x - 9{x}^{2}$

Comparing above equation with general equation of trajectory of projectile $y = x\tan ⁡\theta \left(1 - \frac{x}{R}\right) tan\theta = 2 \implies sin\theta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$ or $cos\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \theta = {sin}^{ - 1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$ or $\theta = {cos}^{ - 1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$

And R = 2/9

$R = \frac{{{v}_{0}}^{2}\sin ⁡2\theta }{g} = \frac{2}{9}$

After substituting the value for g and sin 2θ. We get ${v}_{0} = \frac{3}{5}$ m/s ;

questions.question: Two bodies are projected from ground with same speeds $40m{s}^{ - 1}$ at two different angles with respect to horizontal. The bodies were found to have same range. If one of the body was projected at an angle of $60 ^\circ$, with horizontal then sum of the maximum heights, attained by the two projectiles, is _____ $m$. (Given $g = 10m{s}^{ - 2}$)
questions.explanation:
For two projectiles with same speed to have the same horizontal range, angle of projection will be ${\theta }_{1} + {\theta }_{2} = 90 ^\circ$.

Therefore, ${\theta }_{2} = 90 ^\circ - 60 ^\circ = 30 ^\circ$.

Now, required sum of maximum heights will be,

${\left({H}_{\max }\right)}_{1} + {\left({H}_{\max }\right)}_{2} = \frac{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}{\theta }_{1}}{2g} + \frac{{u}^{2}{\sin }^{2}{\theta }_{2}}{2g} = \frac{{40}^{2}}{20}\left(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{4}\right) = 80m$

questions.question: The projectile motion of a particle of mass $5g$ is shown in the figure. The initial velocity of the particle is $5\sqrt{2}{\mathrm{ms}}^{ - 1}$ and the air resistance is assumed to be negligible. The magnitude of the change in momentum between the points $A$ and $B$ is $x \times {10}^{ - 2}{\mathrm{kgms}}^{ - 1}$. The value of $x$, to the nearest integer, is ___ .
questions.explanation: $| \vec{u} | = | \vec{v} | \vec{u} = u\cos 45\hat{i} + u\sin 45\hat{j} \vec{v} = v\cos 45\hat{i} - \mathrm{vsin}45\hat{j} | \vec{\Delta P} | = \left(m\left(\vec{v} - \vec{u}\right)\right) \Delta P = 2mu\sin 45 ^\circ = 2 \times 5 \times {10}^{ - 3} \times 5\sqrt{2} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Delta P = 50 \times {10}^{ - 3} = 5 \times {10}^{ - 2}$.

questions.question: A particle is projected at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ from horizontal at a speed of $60 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $\mathrm{h}_0$ and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_1$. The ratio $h_0: h_1$ is _________ [Take, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ]
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{S}_1=30 \times 1-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 1=25 \\ & \mathrm{~S}_3=30+\left(\frac{-10}{2}\right) \times(2 \times 3-1)=5 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~S}_1}{\mathrm{~S}_3}=\frac{25}{5}=5\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A body starts falling freely from height $H$ hits an inclined plane in its path at height $h$. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of $\frac{H}{h}$ for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is _____.
questions.explanation: Total time of flight $= T$ can be written as, $T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} + \sqrt{\frac{2\left(H - h\right)}{g}}$ For maximum time $= \frac{dT}{dh} = 0 \implies \sqrt{\frac{2}{g}}\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{h}} - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{H - h}}\right) = 0 \implies \sqrt{H - h} = \sqrt{h} \implies h = \frac{H}{2}\;$

questions.question: An object is projected in the air with initial velocity $u$ at an angle $\theta$. The projectile motion is such that the horizontal range $R$, is maximum. Another object is projected in the air with a horizontal range half of the range of first object. The initial velocity remains same in both the case. The value of the angle of projection, at which the second object is projected, will be _____ degree.
questions.explanation:
The maximum range is given by, ${R}_{\max } = \frac{{u}^{2}\sin 2\left(45 ^\circ \right)}{g} = \frac{{u}^{2}}{g}$.

For the range to be half of the maximum range,

$\frac{{R}_{max}}{2} = \frac{{u}^{2}}{2g} = \frac{{u}^{2}\sin 2\theta }{g} \implies \sin 2\theta = \frac{1}{2} \implies 2\theta = 30 ^\circ \text{or}2\theta = 150 ^\circ \implies \theta = 15 ^\circ ,75 ^\circ$

Therefore, answer is $15\text{or }75$

questions.question: When a car is at rest, its driver sees rain drops falling on it vertically. When driving the car with speed $v$, he sees that rain drops coming at an angle ${60}^{∘}$ from the horizontal. On further increasing the speed of the car to $\left(1 + \beta \right)v$, this angle changes to ${45}^{∘}$. The value of $\beta$ is close to :
questions.explanation: $\tan = 60 ^\circ = \frac{{v}_{\mathrm{rg}}}{v}$ ........$\left(1\right) \tan 45 ^\circ = \frac{{v}_{\mathrm{rg}}}{(\beta + 1)v}$ ..........$\left(2\right) \sqrt{3}v = (\beta + 1)v \beta = \sqrt{3} - 1 = 0.732$

questions.question: At time $t = 0$ a particle starts travelling from a height $7\hat{z}\mathrm{cm}$ in a plane keeping $z$ coordinate constant. At any instant of time, it's position along the $x$ and $y$ directions are defined as $3t$ and $5{t}^{3}$ respectively. At $t = 1s$ acceleration of the particle will be
questions.explanation:
The position vector of the particle can be written as,

$\vec{r} = 3t\hat{i} + 5{t}^{3}\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$

The velocity of the particle will be,

$\vec{v} = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = 3\hat{i} + 15{t}^{2}\hat{j}$

Now the acceleration of the particle will be,

$\vec{a} = \frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = \frac{{d}^{2}\vec{r}}{d{t}^{2}} = 30t\hat{j}$

At $t = 1s \implies \frac{{d}^{2}r}{d{t}^{2}} = 30\hat{j}$

questions.question: A river is flowing from west to east direction with speed of $9 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-1}$. If a boat capable of moving at a maximum speed of $27 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-1}$ in still water, crosses the river in half a minute, while moving with maximum speed at an angle of $150^{\circ}$ to direction of river flow, then the width of the river is :
questions.explanation: $\therefore \mathrm{V}_{\perp}=$ river flow $=27 \times \cos 60^{\circ}=\frac{27}{2} \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$. Time taken $=30 \mathrm{sec}$. $\therefore \mathrm{S}=\mathrm{Vt}=\frac{27}{2} \times \frac{5}{18} \times 30 \mathrm{~m}=112.5 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.question: A butterfly is flying with a velocity $4\sqrt{2}m{s}^{ - 1}$ in north-east direction. Wind is slowly blowing at $1m{s}^{ - 1}$ from north to south. The resultant displacement of the butterfly in $3$ seconds is:
questions.explanation: ${\vec{V}}_{\mathrm{BW}} = 4\sqrt{2}\cos 45\hat{i} + 4\sqrt{2}\sin 45\hat{j} = 4\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} {\vec{V}}_{w} = - \hat{j} {\vec{V}}_{B} = {\vec{V}}_{\mathrm{BW}} + {\vec{V}}_{w} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} {\vec{S}}_{B} = {\vec{V}}_{B} \times t = (4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) \times 3 = 12\hat{i} + 9\hat{j} \left({\vec{S}}_{B}\right) = \sqrt{(12{)}^{2} + (9{)}^{2}} = 15m$ ,

questions.question: The stream of a river is flowing with a speed of $2km{h}^{ - 1}$. A swimmer can swim at a speed of $4\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$. The direction of the swimmer with respect to the flow of the river, to cross the river straight, is
questions.explanation: To reach the point directly opposite to the starting point, the resultant velocity of swimmer should be as shown in figure. From figure $\sin ⁡\theta = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2} \theta = 30 ^\circ$ Angle with flow $= 90 ^\circ + 30 ^\circ = 120 ^\circ$ `

questions.question: In a car race on straight road, car $A$ takes a time $t$ less than car $B$ at the finish and passes finishing point with a speed $v$ more than that of car $B.$ Both the cars start from rest and travel with constant acceleration ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ respectively. Then $v$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Given,

Initially both car is at rest, so ${u}_{1} = {u}_{2} = 0$

Acceleration of car $A & B$ is ${a}_{1} & {a}_{2}$

Let us assume,

Time of reach to destination of car $A$ is, ${t}_{1} = {t}_{0}$

Time of reach to destination of car $B$ is, ${t}_{2} = {t}_{0} + t$

Using second equation of motion, we have

${u}_{1}t + \frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2} = {u}_{2}t + \frac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{{t}_{2}}^{2} \implies 0 \times t + \frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{0}^{2} = 0 \times t + \frac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{\left({t}_{0} + t\right)}^{2} \implies \sqrt{\frac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}}{t}_{0} = {t}_{0} + t \implies {t}_{0} = \frac{t}{\sqrt{\frac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}} - 1}$

From first equation of motion, we have

$\begin{matrix}{v}_{1} = {a}_{1}{t}_{0} & & {v}_{2} = {a}_{2}\left({t}_{0} + t\right)\end{matrix} \implies v = {v}_{1} - {v}_{2} = \left({a}_{1} - {a}_{2}\right){t}_{0} - {a}_{2}t \implies v = \left({a}_{1} - {a}_{2}\right)\frac{t}{\sqrt{\frac{{a}_{1}}{{a}_{2}}} - 1} - {a}_{2}t \implies v = t\left(\frac{{a}_{1}\sqrt{{a}_{2}}}{{\sqrt{a}}_{1} - {\sqrt{a}}_{2}} - \frac{{a}_{2}{\sqrt{a}}_{2}}{{\sqrt{a}}_{1} - {\sqrt{a}}_{2}} - {a}_{2}\right) \implies v = t\left(\frac{{a}_{1}\sqrt{{a}_{2}} - {a}_{2}{\sqrt{a}}_{1}}{{\sqrt{a}}_{1} - {\sqrt{a}}_{2}}\right) \implies v = \sqrt{{a}_{1}.{a}_{2}}t$

!

questions.question: A person is swimming with a speed of $10m{s}^{ - 1}$ at an angle of $120 ^\circ$ with the flow and reaches to a point directly opposite on the other side of the river. The speed of the flow is $xm{s}^{ - 1}.$ The value of $x$ to the nearest integer is ______.

questions.question: A girl standing on road holds her umbrella at $45 ^\circ$ with the vertical to keep the rain away. questions.question: A boy reaches the airport and finds that the escalator is not working. He walks up the stationary escalator in time ${t}_{1}.$ If he remains stationary on a moving escalator then the escalator takes him up in time ${t}_{2}.$ The time taken by him to walk up on the moving escalator will be:

$L =$ Length of escalator

${V}_{b / \mathrm{ecc}} = \frac{L}{{t}_{1}}$

When only escalator is moving,

${V}_{\mathrm{esc}} = \frac{L}{{t}_{2}}$

when both are moving,

${V}_{b / g} = {V}_{b / \mathrm{esc}} + {V}_{\mathrm{esc}} {V}_{b / g} = \frac{L}{{t}_{1}} + \frac{L}{{t}_{2}} \implies \left(t = \frac{L}{{V}_{b / g}} = \frac{{t}_{1}{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}}\right)$

questions.question: A passenger train of length $60m$ travels at a speed of $80\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{hr}$. Another freight train of length $120m$ travels at a speed of $30\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{hr}$. The ratio of times taken by the passenger train to completely cross the freight train when: (i) they are moving in the same direction, and (ii) in the opposite directions is:

options: $5 \sqrt{15} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, making an angle of $\tan ^{-1} 4$ with - ve $Y$ axis

questions.question: The speed of a swimmer is $4\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$ in still water. If the swimmer makes his strokes normal to the flow of river of width $1\mathrm{km}$, he reaches a point $750m$ down the stream on the opposite bank. The speed of the river water is ______ $\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$.
questions.explanation: Let ${v}_{r}$ be velocity of river and ${v}_{m}$ be velocity of man. Time taken by man to cross the river of width $= 1000m$ is $t = \frac{1}{4}h$. Now, drift $x = {v}_{r} \times t \implies 0.750 = {v}_{r} \times \frac{1}{4}\;$

questions.question: A swimmer wants to cross a river from point $A$ to point $B$. Line AB makes an angle of $30 ^\circ$ with the flow of the river. questions.explanation: Both velocity vectors are of same magnitude therefore resultant would pass exactly midway through them $\theta = 30 ^\circ$

questions.question: A block of $200g$ mass moves with a uniform speed in a horizontal circular groove, with vertical side walls of radius $20\mathrm{cm}$. If the block takes $40s$ to complete one round, the normal force by the side walls of the groove is:

questions.question: Two particles $A,B$ are moving on two concentric circles of radii ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ with equal angular speed $\omega .$ At $t = 0,$ their positions and direction of motion are shown in the figure: The relative velocity $\vec{{V}_{A}} - \vec{{V}_{B}}$ at $t = \frac{\pi }{2\omega }$ is given by:
questions.explanation: $t = \frac{\pi }{2\omega }$ ${\vec{V}}_{A} = \omega {R}_{1}\left( - \hat{i}\right) {\vec{V}}_{B} = \omega {R}_{2}\left( - \hat{i}\right) \vec{{V}_{A}} - \vec{{V}_{B}} = \omega \left({R}_{2} - {R}_{1}\right)\hat{i}$

questions.question: A particle moves such that its position vector $\vec{r}\left(t\right) = \cos ⁡\omega t\hat{i} + \sin ⁡\omega t\hat{j}$ where $\omega$ is a constant and $t$ is time. Then which of the following statements is true for the velocity $\vec{v}\left(t\right)$ and acceleration $\vec{a}\left(t\right)$ of the particle:
options: $\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{a}$ is directed away from the origin
$\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{a}$ is directed towards the origin
questions.explanation:
$\vec{r} = \cos ⁡\omega t\hat{i} + \sin ⁡\omega t\hat{j} \vec{v} = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = \omega \left( - \sin ⁡\omega t\hat{i} + \cos ⁡\omega t\hat{j}\right) \vec{a} = \frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = - {\omega }^{2}\left(\cos ⁡\omega t\hat{i} + \sin ⁡\omega t\hat{j}\right) \vec{a} = - {\omega }^{2}\vec{r}∴\vec{a}$ is antiparallel to $\vec{r} \vec{v}.\vec{r} = \omega \left( - \sin ⁡\omega t\cos ⁡\omega t + \cos ⁡\omega t\sin ⁡\omega t\right) = 0$

So $\vec{v}⊥\vec{r}$

questions.question: Motion of a particle in $x - y$ plane is described by a set of following equations $x = 4\sin \left(\frac{\pi }{2} - \omega t\right)m$ and $y = 4\sin \left(\omega t\right)m$. The path of the particle will be
questions.explanation:
$x = 4\sin \left(\frac{\pi }{2} - \omega t\right) = 4\cos \left(\omega t\right)$,

$y = 4\sin \left(\omega t\right)$

Clearly, ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {\left(4\cos \left(\omega t\right)\right)}^{2} + {\left(4\sin \left(\omega t\right)\right)}^{2}\;$

Hence, the path covered by particle is a circle.

.

questions.question: An object moves at a constant speed along a circular path in a horizontal plane with centre at the origin. When the object is at $x = + 2m$, its velocity is $- 4\hat{j}m{s}^{ - 1}$ . The object’s velocity $(v)$ and acceleration $(a)$ at $x = –2m$ will be
questions.explanation: As the speed is constant, only centripetal acceleration will act(towards the centre of the circular path), ${a}_{c} = \frac{{v}^{2}}{r} = \frac{{4}^{2}}{2} = 8m{s}^{ - 2}$ towards the centre which at the given time will be towards right, hence ${\vec{a}}_{c} = 8\hat{i}m{s}^{ - 2}$. Velocity of the particle at this instant will in upward direction and hence $\vec{v} = 4\hat{j}m{s}^{ - 1}$. :

questions.question:
If the angular velocity of earth's spin is increased such that the bodies at the equator start floating, the duration of the day would be approximately :

(Take : $g = 10{\mathrm{ms}}^{ - 2}$, the radius of earth, $R = 6400 \times {10}^{3}m$, Take $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.explanation:
For objects to float,

$mg = m{\omega }^{2}R \omega =$ angular velocity of the earth.

$R =$ Radius of earth

$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{R}}...\left(1\right)$

Duration of day $= T T = \frac{2\pi }{\omega }...\left(2\right) \implies T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{R}{g}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{6400 \times {10}^{3}}{10}} \implies \frac{T}{60} = 83.775$ minutes

$≃84$ minutes

!

${F}_{1} = {F}_{2}\;$

questions.question:
A stone tied to $180\mathrm{cm}$ long string at its end is making $28$ revolutions in horizontal circle in every minute. The magnitude of acceleration of stone is $\frac{1936}{x}m{s}^{ - 2}$. The value of $x$ ______.

$a = {\omega }^{2}R = {\left(\frac{56}{60} \times \frac{22}{7}\right)}^{2} \times 1.8 = \frac{(44{)}^{2}}{225} \times 1.8\;$

Hence, required $x = 125$.

questions.question: A particle is moving along a circular path with a constant speed of $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. What is the magnitude of the change in velocity of the particle, when it moves through an angle of $60^{\circ}$ around the centre of the circle?
questions.explanation: Change in velocity, $$\begin{array}{l} |\Delta \overline{\mathrm{v}}|=\sqrt{\mathrm{v}_{1}^{2}+\mathrm{v}_{2}^{2}+2 \mathrm{v}_{1} \mathrm{v}_{2} \cos (\pi-\theta)} \\ =2 \mathrm{v} \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \quad\left(\because\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{1}\right|=\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{2}\right|\right)=\mathrm{v} \\ =(2 \times 10) \times \sin \left(30^{\circ}\right)=2 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{2} \\ =10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \end{array}$$

questions.question: A man carrying a monkey on his shoulder does cycling smoothly on a circular track of radius $9 \mathrm{~m}$ and completes 120 resolutions in 3 minutes. The magnitude of centripetal acceleration of monkey is $\left(\right.$ in $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ) :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given : } \mathrm{R}=9 \mathrm{~m}, \\ & 120 \text { revolution in } 3 \mathrm{~min} \\ & \omega=\frac{120 \mathrm{Rev} .}{3 \mathrm{~min} .}=\frac{120 \times 2 \pi \mathrm{rad}}{3 \times 60 \mathrm{sec}}=\frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{a}_{\text {centripetal }}=\omega^2 \mathrm{R}=\left(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\right)^2 \times 9=16 \pi^2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A clock has a continuously moving second's hand of $0.1m$ length. The average acceleration of the tip of the hand (in units of ${\mathrm{ms}}^{ - 2}$ ]) is of the order of :
questions.explanation:
The instantaneous acceleration of tip is given by

$\mathrm{ac} = {\omega }^{2}R = {\left(\frac{2\pi }{60}\right)}^{2} \times 0.1 = \frac{1}{900} \approx {10}^{ - 3}$

questions.question: A stone of mass $1\mathrm{kg}$ is tied to end of a massless string of length $1m$. If the breaking tension of the string is $400N$, then maximum linear velocity, the stone can have without breaking the string, while rotating in horizontal plane, is:
questions.explanation:
In horizontal circle, tension towards the centre of the circular path at any moment will provide the required centripetal force.

Therefore,

${T}_{max} = \frac{m{v}^{2}}{r}\;$

.

questions.question:
A boy ties a stone of mass $100g$ to the end of a $2m$ long string and whirls it around in a horizontal plane. The string can withstand the maximum tension of $80N$. If the maximum speed with which the stone can revolve is $\frac{K}{\pi }\mathrm{rev}{\min }^{ - 1}$. The value of $K$ is :

(Assume the string is massless and un-stretchable)

The maximum angular velocity of the stone is $\omega = rpm \times \frac{2\pi }{60} = \frac{K}{30}\mathrm{rad}{s}^{ - 1}$

The tension in the string will provide the required centripetal force. Therefore,

$T = m{\omega }^{2}l\;$

,

questions.question: A vehicle of mass $200\mathrm{kg}$ is moving along a levelled curved road of radius $70m$ with angular velocity of $0.2\mathrm{rad}{s}^{ - 1}$. The centripetal force acting on the vehicle is:
questions.explanation:
The centripetal force is given by

$F = \frac{M{v}^{2}}{R} = MR{\omega }^{2}$

The given data is

$M = 200\mathrm{kg}\;$

The magnitude of the force is

$$$F = 200 \times 70 \times 0.{2}^{2}N \implies F = 560N$

!

questions.question: A ball is spun with angular acceleration $\alpha = 6{t}^{2} - 2t$ where $t$ is in second and $\alpha$ is in $\mathrm{rad}{s}^{ - 2}$. At $t = 0$, the ball has angular velocity of $10\mathrm{rad}{s}^{ - 1}$ and angular position of $4\mathrm{rad}$. The most appropriate expression for the angular position of the ball is
questions.explanation:
Given: $\alpha = 6{t}^{2} - 2t$

Using relation $\alpha = \frac{d\omega }{dt} = 6{t}^{2} - 2t$

Integrating the above,

${ \int }_{10}^{\omega }d\omega = { \int }_{0}^{t}\left(6{t}^{2} - 2t\right)dt \implies \omega - 10 = 2{t}^{3} - {t}^{2}$

Now, $\omega = \frac{d\theta }{dt} = 10 + 2{t}^{3} - {t}^{2} { \int }_{4}^{\theta }d\theta = { \int }_{0}^{t}\left(10 + 2{t}^{3} - {t}^{2}\right)dt$

Integrating the above relation,

$\theta - 4 = 10t + \frac{{t}^{4}}{2} - \frac{{t}^{3}}{3}$

Thus, angular position of the ball is $\theta = \frac{{t}^{4}}{2} - \frac{{t}^{3}}{3} + 10t + 4$.

;

questions.question: A car is moving on a circular path of radius $600m$ such that the magnitudes of the tangential acceleration and centripetal acceleration are equal. The time taken by the car to complete first quarter of revolution, if it is moving with an initial speed of $54\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$ is $t(1–{e}^{–\frac{\pi }{2}})s$. The value of $t$ is ______.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Initial speed $= \frac{54 \times 1000}{3600} = 15m{s}^{ - 1} \left({a}_{t}\right) = \left({a}_{c}\right) \implies v\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{{v}^{2}}{R}\; \implies v = 15{e}^{\frac{x}{R}} \implies \frac{dx}{dt} = 15{e}^{\frac{x}{R}}$

Distance covered in first quarter of revolution $= \frac{2\pi R}{4} = \frac{\pi R}{2}$.

Therefore,

${ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi R}{2}}{e}^{ - \frac{x}{R}}dx = 15{ \int }_{0}^{{t}_{0}}dt \implies {t}_{0} = 40\left(1 - {e}^{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}\right)$

Hence, $t = 40$.

questions.question: A bead of mass $m$ stays at point $P\left(a,b\right)$ on a wire bent in the shape of a parabola $y = 4C{x}^{2}$ and rotating with angular speed $\omega$ (see figure). The value of $\omega$ is (neglect friction)

questions.question: The distance of the Sun from earth is $1.5 \times {10}^{11}m$ and its angular diameter is $2000''$ when observed from the earth. The diameter of the Sun will be
questions.explanation: Diameter of Sun is $D = r\theta \begin{matrix} = 1.5 \times {10}^{11} \times (2000) \times \left(\frac{1}{3600}\right) \times \left(\frac{\pi }{180}\right) \\ = 1.45 \times {10}^{9}m\end{matrix}$

questions.question: A child of mass $5\mathrm{kg}$ is going round a merry-go-round that makes $1$ rotation in $3.14s$. The radius of the merry-go-round is $2m$. The centrifugal force on the child will be
questions.explanation:
The angular speed $\left(\omega \right)$ of the child can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{matrix}\omega & = & \frac{2\pi }{3.14} \\ = 2\mathrm{rad}{s}^{ - 1}\end{matrix}$

The formula to calculate the centrifugal force on the child is given by

${F}_{r} = m{\omega }^{2}r...(1)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required centrifugal force.

$\begin{matrix}{F}_{r} & = & 5\mathrm{kg} \times {\left(2\mathrm{rad}{s}^{ - 1}\right)}^{2} \times 2m \\ = 40N\end{matrix}$

questions.question: A particle is moving with constant speed in a circular path. When the particle turns by an angle $90 ^\circ ,$ the ratio of instantaneous velocity to its average velocity is $\pi : x\sqrt{2}.$ The value of $x$ will be
questions.explanation: In circular motion with constant speed, magnitude of instantaneous velocity, ${v}_{ins} = \omega r$. Time taken to turn by $90 ^\circ$ will be $= \frac{\frac{\pi }{2}}{\omega } = \frac{\pi }{2\omega }$. Displacement will be equal to the length of $AB = \sqrt{{r}^{2} + {r}^{2}} = r\sqrt{2}$ Average velocity ${v}_{avg} = \frac{\text{displacement}}{\text{time}}\;$ Hence, required ratio $\frac{{v}_{\text{ins }}}{{v}_{\text{avg }}} = \frac{\omega r\pi }{2\sqrt{2}\omega r} = \frac{\pi }{2\sqrt{2}}$ Therefore, $x = 2$.

questions.question: A disc is rolling without slipping on a surface. The radius of the disc is $R.$ At $t = 0,$ the top most point on the disc is $A$ as shown in figure. When the disc completes half of its rotation, the displacement of point $A$ from its initial position is
questions.explanation: The displacement is the hypotenuse of the diameter and the distance travelled for half the rotation $\pi R$. By using Pythagoras theorem, Displacement of $A = \sqrt{(2R{)}^{2} + (\pi R{)}^{2}} = R\sqrt{{\pi }^{2} + 4}$
